Jordan — appreciate the examples, this is a good catch and common for streaming-first integrations. High level:

1) Billing quantum (short responses): we bill tokens in quanta configured per-SKU. For your current pilot SKU the quantum is 100 tokens per billed request, which reduces per-token bookkeeping complexity and protects against high-cardinality micro-charging. So any streaming write that ends up as a discrete billed request will be rounded up to the 100-token quantum.

2) Microbursts optimization: we have a prefix/KV cache that reduces compute and latency when the same prefix is reused, but currently caching does not reduce the billed token count unless the request exactly hits a cached response from our templating layer (rare). That said, we're rolling out a beta that credits repeated identical prefixes — we can include you if desired.

3) Long-history chunking: when a single logical conversation exceeds the model window and we split it into multiple prompt chunks, the billing is per-chunk (i.e., each chunk consumes billed tokens). We do perform a best-effort merge when chunks are strictly sequential with shared KV state, but that does not change token accounting — it reduces compute but not billed units.

I'll let Kimberly drop the worked math on your attached invoice and propose a remediation if we mis-applied pilot concession.

— Rishi Malhotra
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Jordan — thanks for the invoice and CSV. I ran the numbers and attached a short calculation spreadsheet (calculation_spreadsheet.xlsx) showing how the three bursts were billed. Summary:

- Per your pilot SKU the minimum billed quantum is 100 tokens per request. Your bursts (12/9/5 tokens) were each individual streaming requests; because we bill the finalised request size and then apply the quantum, each was rounded up to 100 tokens. That matches the invoice lines you saw.

Worked example (from the spreadsheet):
• Burst A3 — actual tokens 12 -> billed 100 (quantum)
• Burst A7 — actual tokens 9 -> billed 100
• Burst A9 — actual tokens 5 -> billed 100

- Long conversation split: for the session where you exceeded 16k we show two prompt chunks at 10.7k and 7.1k tokens respectively. Both were billed as separate prompt tokens plus the generated output tokens; total = billed tokens for chunk1 + chunk2. There's no amortized single-unit billing for chunked prompts.

Proposed remediation options:
1) Credit: we can apply a one-time credit for up to 300 tokens for the pilot month while you evaluate streaming behavior (manual invoice adjustment).
2) Pilot tweak: move DatumHealth to a micro-quantum SKU (25-token quantum) for the next billing month at no additional charge — this reduces rounding overhead for microbursts.

If you want the credit we can start the DocuSign amendment (link below) and apply the credit on the next invoice; if you prefer the micro-quantum trial we can enable it immediately and backdate to June 1st for evaluation.
